# UPI-OVERVIEW: UPI ecosystem and participant roles
URL: https://eyeinthesky6.github.io/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/upi-ecosystem/
Description: UPI-OVERVIEW — system architecture, participant boundaries, and asymmetric risk telemetry.
Product: upi | Type: explainer | Review Stage: source-checked | Last Source Check: 2026-11-23
Actors: npci, remitter-bank, beneficiary-bank, psp-bank, tpap, payment-aggregator, merchant | Evidence Layers: official, atlas

## What it covers
Unified Payments Interface (UPI) runs across separate banks, TPAP apps, Payment Aggregators, and NPCI rather than inside a single institution. Authentication, fraud monitoring, merchant onboarding, settlement reconciliation, and dispute resolution are split—each participant sees only its own slice of customer, device, and payment telemetry.

## Participant roles at a glance

| Participant | Telemetry typically visible | Blind spots | Core control ownership |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Remitter (Issuer) Bank** | Account tenure, historical outflows, PIN/auth checks, SMS alert replies | Third-party TPAP UI screens, client-side screen sharing | Authentication, outbound velocity/EFRM, customer liability, NCRP coordination |
| **Beneficiary Bank** | Payee KYC, credit inflows, onward fan-out / ATM cash-outs, shared branch/address ties | Payer's pre-payment social-engineering context | Mule-funnel detection (`MuleHunter.AI`), inflow alerts, `T+1` failed-credit reversals |
| **PSP Bank / TPAP** | VPA mapping, device/SIM binding, runtime/screen-share checks, intent metadata | Customer balance/income across unlinked banks | Mobile app security/audits, debit-direction UX clarity, in-app ODR initiation |
| **Acquiring Bank / PA** | Merchant KYC/CPV, MCC, checkout volume, chargebacks, webhook status | Payer's handset security or phone-call coercion | Merchant CDD/MCC vetting, profile-drift monitoring, escrow/dispute flows |

## Key obligations and boundaries

| Basis | Owner | Rule / operational boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory | NPCI & Non-bank PSOs | NPCI is regulated as a Large non-bank PSO (effective Nov 5, 2026; Small PSOs effective Apr 1, 2028); risk with unregulated ecosystem links is governed via agreements rather than identical bank mandates. Under NPCI scheme rules, NPCI frames operating, settlement, and dispute cutoffs while approving banks and TPAPs. |
| Regulatory | Commercial, PB & Small Finance banks | Banks follow separate entity-scoped RBI Digital Payment Security Controls covering MFA, EFRM alert parameters, 24-hour settlement reconciliation, and mobile app binding. |
| Regulatory | Domestic Payment Providers & Participants | RBI's 2025 Authentication Directions apply across domestic payment providers/participants (with explicit recurring e-mandate and Tap-and-Pay UPI exemptions), placing compliance responsibility on issuers. |
| Regulatory | PSP Banks & UPI Apps (TPAPs) | Under NPCI role rules, **PSP Banks** connect TPAP apps/merchants, onboard/link accounts, enforce app security audits, keep UPI transaction data exclusively in India, and handle grievances; **TPAPs** operate through sponsor PSP banks and must offer in-app ODR dispute lodging. |
| Regulatory | Payment Aggregators & Acquiring Banks | RBI's PA Master Direction assigns merchant KYC/CDD, MCC accuracy, profile monitoring, and escrow governance to PAs while keeping acquiring banks responsible for policy oversight. |
| Atlas guidance | Product & risk architects | Map every fraud or recon rule explicitly to its owning institution, required signals, and cross-entity handoff SLA so checks don't silently fall between TPAP and bank boundaries. |

## Watch-outs
- **Double-blocking & blind spots:** Uncoordinated heuristics across TPAPs, issuer banks, and beneficiary banks can stack conflicting friction or prolong erroneous freezes with unclear unblocking ownership.
- **No single-entity rulebooks:** Never assume a bank obligation applies identically to a TPAP or Small PSO without verifying entity class and effective dates.

## References and review history
1. RBI, [Master Directions on Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank PSOs](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13751&Mode=0), `RBI/DPSS/2026-27/475` (Nov 5, 2026; `§§3–5`, footnote 1 — Large/Medium immediate, Small Apr 1, 2028), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
2. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13642), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/411` (`Ch. I §3`, updated Oct 1, 2026 — excludes SFBs/PBs/LABs), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
3. RBI, [Payments Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13624), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/429` (`Ch. I §3`, updated Oct 1, 2026), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
4. RBI, [Small Finance Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13633) (`Ch. I §3`, updated Oct 1, 2026), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
5. RBI, [Authentication Mechanisms for Digital Payment Transactions Directions, 2025](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12898&Mode=0), `RBI/2025-26/79` (Sep 25, 2025; `§§3–4, §9`, `Annexure-1`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
6. RBI, [Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregator (PA)](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=12896), `RBI/DPSS/2025-26/141` (updated Nov 11, 2026; `§§3, 13–14, 16–18`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.

# UPI-001: Unusual outbound payment velocity
URL: https://eyeinthesky6.github.io/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/unusual-outbound-velocity/
Description: UPI-001 — account-level outbound burst and rapid balance-depletion signals.
Product: upi | Type: detective-control | Review Stage: source-checked | Last Source Check: 2026-11-23
Actors: remitter-bank, psp-bank, tpap, payment-aggregator | Evidence Layers: official, research, atlas

## What it solves
Detects sudden bursts of outgoing UPI payments—such as multiple back-to-back transfers to unfamiliar payees, rapid splitting right after an incoming credit, or abrupt balance draining—early enough to flag account takeover, scam coercion, or mule cash-outs. Outbound velocity is a **risk signal, not standalone proof of fraud**.

## Impact when missing
- **Customer:** Victim balances or compromised accounts are drained across multiple rapid hops before alerts are reviewed.
- **Banks & PSPs:** Counting raw transfers without comparing against the customer's own baseline misses stealth draining or floods queues with noisy retail alerts.

## When it applies
- Multiple outbound UPI debits or new beneficiary additions compressed into a short window.
- First-time mobile/UPI channel usage on an established account, or excessive burst activity right after account opening.
- Outbound bursts immediately following a new device link or an unfamiliar large credit.

*(For program-wide EFRM governance, staffing, and alert-tuning obligations, see [Transaction velocity and EFRM monitoring](/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/transaction-velocity/).)*

## What to do (rules and controls)

| Basis | Owner | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory | Commercial, Payments & Small Finance banks | Parameterize monitoring alerts for transaction velocity (electronic fund transfers and new beneficiary additions in short periods), first-time mobile/internet channel usage, and excessive new-account activity. RBI sets no fixed rupee/count cutoff—banks document risk-based limits. |
| Regulatory | Non-bank PSOs | Maintain real-time/near-real-time fraud monitoring and facilitate online participant alerts for velocity and new-account spikes (effective immediately for Large/Medium PSOs; Apr 1, 2028 for Small PSOs). |
| Research & academic | Risk & ML teams | An Indian RBIH NFPC study found alternating high-velocity outbound runs paired with prior inflows and dormancy separated mules from legitimate bursts that revert quickly to baseline. |
| Research & academic | Fraud product teams | An empirical GPay India evaluation achieving >88% recall saw ~30% precision on evaluated splits—meaning behavioral velocity triggers alone create too many false blocks if wired directly to hard freezes without step-up or review. |
| Atlas guidance | Remitter banks, PSPs, TPAPs | Score rolling 15-minute, 1-hour, and 24-hour outbound counts, value, balance depletion share, and unique-new-payee ratio relative to each account's own 30/90-day baseline; prioritize bursts paired with recent device binding or unfamiliar inflows. |

## Watch-outs and validation
- **Legitimate lookalikes:** Small merchants paying suppliers at day-end, festive shopping/gifting, group-trip splits, salary-day family transfers, and active new users. Prefer step-up confirmation or scoped temporary holds over blanket account freezes.
- **Signals needed:** Timestamps, debit/credit direction, outcome status, amount, pre/post balance, anonymized counterparty VPA/account ID, account tenure, and device/session context.
- **How to validate:** Measure alert `precision@k` at your real daily analyst queue capacity, track false-positive overturn rates by segment (merchant vs retail), and stress-test against salary-week and festival spikes.

## References and review history
1. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13642), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/411` (updated Oct 1, 2026) — documented rule configuration (`§52`) and monitoring parameters (`§53`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
2. RBI, [Payments Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13624), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/429` (updated Oct 1, 2026; `§§52–53`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
3. RBI, [Small Finance Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13633) (updated Oct 1, 2026; `§§52–53`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
4. RBI, [Master Directions on Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank PSOs](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13751&Mode=0), `RBI/DPSS/2026-27/475` (Nov 5, 2026; `§§3, 27(c), 28`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
5. Ahmad, O. & Deodhar, A. (2026), [Money-Mule Detection as a Relational Learning Problem: A Study on the RBIH NFPC Dataset](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.21314v1), `arXiv:2610.21314v1` (`§4, Fig. 2`) — Indian benchmark study (narrow scope, not a turnkey cutoff), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
6. Dahiphale, D. et al. / Google, Inc. (2024), [Enhancing Trust and Safety in Digital Payments: An LLM-Powered Approach](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.19845v1), `arXiv:2410.19845v1` (`§V-A`) — GPay India empirical study, accessed Nov 23, 2026.

**Review status:** RBI and `arXiv` sources checked 2026-11-23; independent reviewer: `PENDING`.

# UPI-002: Potential mule-account funnel
URL: https://eyeinthesky6.github.io/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/mule-account-funnel/
Description: UPI-002 — pass-through layering networks, RBIH MuleHunter.AI / I4C coordination, and relational detection limits.
Product: upi | Type: fraud-pattern | Review Stage: source-checked | Last Source Check: 2026-11-23
Actors: beneficiary-bank, remitter-bank, psp-bank, payment-aggregator | Evidence Layers: official, research, atlas

## What it is
Money mules receive fraud proceeds from unrelated victims and quickly forward them onward across other bank accounts, wallets, or cash-outs. On its own, each UPI transaction can look like normal retail spend—the giveaway is **tight inflow-to-outflow coupling, sudden activity after dormancy, and shared infrastructure** (devices, addresses, IP/branch attributes) tying separate accounts together.

## Impact
- **Beneficiary & remitter banks:** High alert backlogs, NCRP lien/freeze coordination overhead, and regulatory scrutiny on mule onboarding.
- **Innocent sellers & community accounts:** Broad or blunt freezes lock up legitimate livelihoods when normal merchants receive a tainted scam transfer.
- **Ecosystem recovery:** Every extra hop delays inter-bank tracing and lowers funds recoverable after fraud reporting.

## Common patterns
- **Dormant-to-burst pass-through:** A low-balance or inactive account receives multiple inbound credits and immediately drains onward.
- **Shared-entity mule rings:** Separate customer accounts reuse underlying phone numbers, addresses, postal PINs, counterparties, or devices.
- **Layered cross-rail cash-out:** Inbound UPI credits rapidly scatter across linked UPI handles, cards, or ATM withdrawals.

## What to do (rules and mitigations)

| Basis | Owner | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory | Commercial, Payments & Small Finance banks | Monitor new-account activity spikes, rapid velocity, beneficiary additions, and transfers to VPAs/mobile numbers linked to recorded frauds; maintain stakeholder coordination SOPs. |
| Regulatory | Commercial, Payments & Small Finance banks | Run Data Analytics/MI digital transaction monitoring and EWS frameworks; follow natural-justice due process (21-day Show Cause Notice and reasoned order) before formal fraud classification. |
| Regulatory | Banks, I4C, RBIH | Coordinate NCRP Suspect Registry intelligence with RBIH `MuleHunter.AI`; RBI's Apr 2026 discussion paper also consults on monitoring credits against KYC profile (non-binding). |
| Research & academic | Risk & ML teams | On the Indian RBIH NFPC dataset (~237.8M txns across 96,091 accounts), GBDTs (`XGBoost`/`LightGBM`) achieved 96–99% precision for tiny daily queues (`k=100`), whereas temporal heterogeneous GNNs outperformed GBDTs at deeper queues (`k=500`) by capturing 2-to-4-hop shared counterparties, addresses, and PINs. |
| Research & academic | Investigation teams | An OCBC Singapore study combined 280 account features, LightGBM, TreeSHAP, and constrained LLM case narratives to lift investigator alert yield from 61% to 89% (non-India AML comparison; dataset limits apply). |
| Atlas guidance | Banks, PAs | Score inflow/outflow ratio, onward-debit latency, fan-in/fan-out diversity, and shared device/address attributes; isolate only contested funds where permitted instead of freezing entire livelihood accounts blindly. |

## Watch-outs and validation
- **Legitimate lookalikes:** Community or housing-society collections, micro-merchants/kiranas, gig-worker payouts, and innocent sellers who unwittingly accepted payment from a scam victim.
- **Positive-unlabelled feedback trap:** Treating every uninvestigated account as "confirmed clean" teaches models to treat undetected mule rings as normal behavior.
- **Signals needed:** KYC profile/account age, credit-debit latency pairs, anonymized counterparty graph edges, shared contact/address indicators, NCRP Suspect Registry hits, and investigator dispositions.
- **How to validate:** Enforce strict per-account time cutoffs (`τ(v) <= t_seed`) to stop future label leakage, evaluate `precision@k` at your real daily analyst queue size, and audit overturned freezes separately from confirmed fraud.

## References and review history
1. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13642), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/411` — fraud-linked monitoring parameters (`§53`) and stakeholder coordination SOPs (`§56`), accessed Nov 23, 2026 (parallel `id=13624` PBs, `id=13633` SFBs).
2. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13641) (Jul 2026) — digital analytics/MI (`§25`), EWS/RFA (`§12`), and 21-day Show Cause Notice + reasoned order (`§6`), accessed Nov 23, 2026 (parallel `id=13623` PBs, `id=13632` SFBs).
3. RBI, [Discussion Paper – Exploring safeguards in digital payments to curb frauds](https://www.rbi.org.in/scriptS/PublicationsView.aspx?id=23810) (Apr 9, 2026; non-binding consultation) — NCRP SOP, `MuleHunter.AI` context (`§§viii–ix`), and KYC-commensurate credit monitoring (`Option 3`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
4. PIB / Government of India, [I4C and RBIH MoU on MuleHunter.AI](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2260277&reg=3&lang=2) — confirms Suspect Registry data-sharing MoU, accessed Nov 23, 2026.
5. Ahmad, O. & Deodhar, A. (2026), [Money-Mule Detection as a Relational Learning Problem: A Study on the RBIH NFPC Dataset](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.21314v1), `arXiv:2610.21314v1` (`§§1, 5, 7.2, 8`) — Indian NFPC benchmark & PU-bias analysis (academic research lead, not a ready-to-use bank threshold), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
6. Zhang, Y. et al. / OCBC Singapore (2026), [Detection, Attribution, Narration: An End-to-End Pipeline for Explainable Money Mule Identification](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.17586v1), `arXiv:2607.17586v1` — non-India AML explainability study, accessed Nov 23, 2026.

**Review status:** RBI, PIB, and `arXiv` sources checked 2026-11-23; independent reviewer: `PENDING`.

# UPI-003: Account takeover and device-binding risk
URL: https://eyeinthesky6.github.io/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/account-takeover/
Description: UPI-003 — unauthorized account/device compromise, SIM/device binding, and post-change cooling periods.
Product: upi | Type: fraud-pattern | Review Stage: source-checked | Last Source Check: 2026-11-23
Actors: payer, tpap, psp-bank, remitter-bank | Evidence Layers: official, atlas

## What it is
Account takeover (ATO) happens when an attacker steals control of a customer's mobile number, SIM, UPI app login, or credentials and uses that access to drain the account. While bank device checks have reduced pure technical takeovers relative to manipulation scams, silent SIM swaps, recycled mobile numbers, and malware-based re-registration still create high-speed losses.

## Impact
- **Customer:** Rapid unauthorized transfers shortly after a SIM swap, device switch, or mobile-number change.
- **Bank & PSP:** Sudden shift from trusted-device activity to risky transfers and zero-warning dispute liability checks.
- **Legitimate users:** Overly rigid device checks after genuine phone upgrades, lost SIM replacements, or travel can lock victims out during emergencies.

## Common patterns
- **SIM swap & silent re-binding:** Attackers transfer the victim's mobile number to a new SIM and re-register UPI on an unfamiliar handset.
- **Recycled or disconnected mobile numbers:** Reassigned MSISDNs expose dormant accounts or linked VPAs if telecom revocation lists are not checked.
- **Post-change draining:** Credentials or phone numbers are updated and followed immediately by high-value or first-time-channel payouts.

## What to do (rules and mitigations)

| Basis | Owner | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory | Commercial, Payments & Small Finance banks | Bind mobile apps to hardware, software, and service identifiers; require re-auth at launch and after inactivity; block access when remote-access apps are detected; monitor first-time channel, IP, geo, and behavioral anomalies. |
| Regulatory | Non-bank PSOs | Enforce binding tied to both device and SIM (with re-binding after prolonged disuse), plus a minimum 12-hour cooling period for online payments after any mobile-number or email change. |
| Atlas guidance | Banks, TPAPs, PSPs | Screen customer mobile numbers against the DoT Mobile Number Revocation List (MNRL) to catch disconnected or reassigned numbers early. |
| Atlas guidance | Banks, TPAPs | Send instant out-of-band alerts on new device linkages, and apply step-up checks when a newly bound device attempts immediate high-value transfers. |

## Watch-outs and validation
- **Legitimate lookalikes:** Phone upgrades, lost-phone replacement SIMs, dual-SIM handsets, carrier roaming, OS updates altering device fingerprints, and VPN traffic. Always provide clear alerts and documented recovery paths alongside cooling periods.
- **Signals needed:** Device fingerprint, SIM/IMSI change markers, MSISDN/email update timestamps, IP/ASN & coarse location history, remote-access/emulator flags, and auth attempt logs.
- **How to validate:** Test cooling-period enforcement in staging after SIM/contact updates, verify out-of-band delivery of new-device alerts, and track support tickets plus false-block overturn rates after OS or SIM upgrades.

## References and review history
1. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13642), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/411` (updated Oct 1, 2026) — device binding (`§68(6)`), session/launch re-auth (`§68(8)`), remote-access login prohibition (`§68(2)(iv)`), anomaly monitoring (`§53`), and device/limit/PIN change alerts (`§46`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
2. RBI, [Payments Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13624), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/429` (updated Oct 1, 2026) — parallel bank controls, accessed Nov 23, 2026.
3. RBI, [Small Finance Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13633) (updated Oct 1, 2026) — parallel SFB controls, accessed Nov 23, 2026.
4. RBI, [Master Directions on Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank PSOs](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13751&Mode=0), `RBI/DPSS/2026-27/475` (Nov 5, 2026; Large/Medium effective immediately, Small effective Apr 1, 2028 per `§3`) — device+SIM binding (`§31(c)`) and 12-hour contact-change cooling period (`§31(g)`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
5. RBI, [Discussion Paper – Exploring safeguards in digital payments to curb frauds](https://www.rbi.org.in/scriptS/PublicationsView.aspx?id=23810) (Apr 9, 2026; non-binding consultation) — DoT MNRL usage (`§vii`) and observation that technical ATO fraud is relatively small compared to APP scams (`§x`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.

**Review status:** RBI primary sources checked 2026-11-23; independent reviewer: `PENDING`.

# UPI-004: Collect-request deception
URL: https://eyeinthesky6.github.io/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/collect-request-deception/
Description: UPI-004 — social engineering around payment direction, P2P collect discontinuation, and P2M pull controls.
Product: upi | Type: fraud-pattern | Review Stage: source-checked | Last Source Check: 2026-11-23
Actors: payer, tpap, psp-bank, remitter-bank, merchant | Evidence Layers: official, industry, atlas

## What it is
A scammer sends a UPI payment request and tricks the victim into thinking that approving the popup and entering their UPI PIN will *credit* money into their account. Because authorization prompts can look routine when someone is rushed or coached on a call, victims unknowingly approve money *leaving* their account.

## Impact
- **Customer:** Immediate, real-time debit that the victim authorized under deception, leading to disputed recovery.
- **Bank & PSP:** High APP-scam complaint load and regulatory liability exposure where clear, specific scam warnings were missing.
- **Merchant & App:** Legitimate merchant pull checkouts lose trust and conversion when users fear collect popups.

## Common patterns
- **Fake marketplace buyer:** A buyer pretends to send payment for a listed item and instead sends a collect request.
- **Fake refund or prize:** A caller tells the customer to approve a pending prompt and enter their UPI PIN to receive cashback or a refund.
- **Urgency coaching:** The scammer stays on the line rushing the victim past the screen before they check payment direction.

## What to do (rules and mitigations)

| Basis | Owner | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory | Banks, PSPs, Apps | Discontinue all Person-to-Person (P2P) UPI Collect requests (banned beyond Oct 1, 2025). Keep only Merchant (P2M) collect flows active. |
| Regulatory | Commercial banks | Treat deception- or coercion-induced approvals as fraudulent transactions (effective Jan 1, 2027), and record whether directed scam warnings were shown and ignored. |
| Industry practice | Merchants, PAs | Favor app-to-app UPI Intent over Collect in mobile checkouts; keep P2M Collect and Dynamic QR mostly for desktop checkouts and exempted flows such as IPO mandates. |
| Atlas guidance | PSPs, Issuer banks | Enforce P2P collect blocks at the switch and PSP layers, and verify merchant MID/MCC records before routing any pull request. |
| Atlas guidance | UPI Apps, Banks | Show unmistakable debit framing ("Paying Rs X to verified merchant — money leaves your account") with higher-friction warnings on unusual collect prompts. |

## Watch-outs and validation
- **Legitimate lookalikes:** Desktop e-commerce checkouts, recurring utility or subscription bills, and IPO ASBA-via-UPI mandates where the payer expects a pull request.
- **Signals needed:** Initiation channel (`P2P` vs `P2M` collect vs `intent`), payee VPA/MID/MCC, payer-payee prior history, device/app context, and notification timing.
- **How to validate:** Run negative switch tests confirming P2P collect requests fail cleanly, test user comprehension of debit-direction screens, and track drop-off vs. scam loss when warnings trigger.

## References and review history
1. NPCI, [`NPCI/UPI/OC/220/2025-26`: Discontinuing the service of UPI Collect Request for Person to Person (P2P) transactions](https://www.npci.org.in/uploads/UPI_OC_No_220_FY_2025_26_Discontinuing_the_service_of_UPI_Collect_Request_for_Person_to_Person_P2_P_transactions_3fb30c60d7.pdf) (Jul 29, 2025; effective Oct 1, 2025) — applies to member banks, PSPs, and TPAPs/UPI Apps; P2M Collect remains distinct (browser-checked Nov 23, 2026).
2. NPCI, [UPI Circulars index](https://www.npci.org.in/circulars/upi) — searched 2025–2026 circulars via browser on Nov 23, 2026; no public circular restricting mobile manual VPA checkout fields was listed.
3. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Responsible Business Conduct Third Amendment Directions, 2026](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13543&Mode=0), `RBI/2026-27/167` (Jun 24, 2026; effective Jan 1, 2027) — applies to commercial banks excluding SFBs, PBs, RRBs, and LABs (`§§3(2), 4(15A), 4(20C)(iii)`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
4. Razorpay, [UPI Intent vs Collect: Which Flow Actually Works Better in 2026?](https://razorpay.com/blog/upi-intent-vs-collect-success-rates/) (Apr 9, 2026) — company-reported guide noting Feb 2026 mobile-VPA restrictions (attributed solely to Razorpay pending public NPCI circular listing), accessed Nov 23, 2026.

**Review status:** Official NPCI `OC/220/2025-26`, RBI `RBI/2026-27/167`, and Razorpay sources checked 2026-11-23; independent reviewer: `PENDING`.

# UPI-005: Payment status and order reconciliation
URL: https://eyeinthesky6.github.io/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/payment-status-reconciliation/
Description: UPI-005 — merchant/PA payment status, webhook authenticity, idempotency, and order-fulfilment reconciliation.
Product: upi | Type: operational-failure | Review Stage: source-checked | Last Source Check: 2026-11-23
Actors: payment-aggregator, merchant, psp-bank, remitter-bank, beneficiary-bank | Evidence Layers: official, industry, atlas

## What it is
In online UPI merchant checkouts, the customer's browser screen, redirect `callback_url`, asynchronous Payment Aggregator (PA) webhook, and bank settlement file are four separate states. Order fulfillment breaks when merchants trust unverified browser redirects, process retried webhooks as second payments, leave orders permanently stuck in `PENDING`, or send duplicate refunds. *(For interbank settlement-file matching and `T+1`/`T+5` reversal SLAs, see [Settlement and reconciliation exceptions](/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/settlement-exceptions/).)*

## Impact
- **Customer:** Account gets debited while the order stays failed or cancelled, locking funds until `T+5` auto-reversal or manual refund.
- **Merchant:** Double shipment of goods or duplicate payouts when retried webhooks are not deduplicated.
- **PA & Acquirer:** Unmatched order vs escrow records violate PA payout transparency and refund rules.

## Common failure modes
- **Browser callback spoofing / drop-off:** Customer closes the browser before redirect returns, or an attacker spoofs query parameters on an unverified `callback_url`.
- **Duplicate / out-of-order webhooks:** At-least-once delivery or `order.paid` arriving before `payment.captured` triggers double fulfillment or false state regressions.
- **Stuck `PENDING` auto-cancellation:** Premature cron job cancels a paid order whose webhook arrived slow, causing support complaints.

## What to do (rules and controls)

| Basis | Owner | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory | Payment Aggregators, Merchants, Acquirers | Define clear failed-transaction and refund terms in PA/merchant/acquirer agreements; settle merchant balances transparently with day-end escrow adequacy, and route refunds/reversals through escrow unless merchant-managed with payer clarity. |
| Regulatory | Banks, Non-bank PSOs | Auto-reverse debited-but-unconfirmed merchant UPI transactions within `T+5` calendar days (`₹100/day` customer compensation beyond `T+5`). |
| Industry practice | Merchants, PAs | Verify HMAC-SHA256 webhook signatures on raw bytes (`X-Razorpay-Signature`, or Cashfree `x-webhook-signature` + `x-webhook-timestamp`) before parsing JSON; acknowledge within 5 seconds, deduplicate on unique event IDs (`x-razorpay-event-id` / `x-idempotency-header`), and use dedicated idempotency headers on refund/payout retries *(Razorpay & Cashfree documented patterns)*. |
| Atlas guidance | Merchants, Checkout teams | Store verified webhook events atomically before returning `2xx`, drive fulfillment through a strict order state machine (`created -> authorized/paid -> settled` or `failed`) keyed to `order_id` + `payment_id`/UTR, and poll server-side status + daily settlement reports before cancelling `PENDING` orders. |

## Watch-outs and validation
- **Legitimate lookalikes:** Duplicate webhook retries after a slow `2xx` response, transient mobile network timeouts, and out-of-order capture/settlement webhooks are normal delivery behavior—never flag them as fraud or double debits.
- **Signals needed:** Raw HTTP request body, signature and timestamp headers, provider event ID, merchant `order_id`, gateway `payment_id`, RRN/UTR, and daily settlement report rows.
- **How to validate:** Replay duplicate and out-of-order webhook fixtures in staging, confirm 1-byte body tamper returns HTTP `400`, and test reconciliation jobs against unmatched `PENDING` orders and settlement files.

## References and review history
1. RBI, [Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregator (PA)](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=12896), `RBI/DPSS/2025-26/141` (updated Nov 11, 2026) — failed-transaction & refund contracts (`§8(b)`), escrow adequacy (`§16`), and escrow refund routing (`§18(h)`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
2. RBI, [Harmonisation of Turn Around Time (TAT) and customer compensation for failed transactions](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=11693&Mode=0), `RBI/2019-20/67` (Sep 20, 2019; `Sl. no. 4(b)`) — `T+5` auto-reversal and `₹100/day` compensation, accessed Nov 23, 2026.
3. Razorpay, [Payment Gateway Webhooks: Signatures, Retries & Logs](https://razorpay.com/blog/payment-gateway-webhooks-india/) (Oct 27, 2026) — company-reported 5s timeout, 24h backoff, raw-body HMAC, event deduplication, 7-day replay, and `X-Refund-Idempotency` / `X-Payout-Idempotency` headers, accessed Nov 23, 2026.
4. Cashfree Docs, [Webhooks Overview](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/online/webhooks/overview) & [Webhook Verification](https://www.cashfree.com/devstudio/preview/pg/tools/webhookVerification) — company-reported `x-webhook-signature`, `x-idempotency-header` (`2025-01-01`), and default 2/10/30 min retries, accessed Nov 23, 2026.

**Review status:** RBI, Razorpay, and Cashfree sources checked 2026-11-23; independent reviewer: `PENDING`.

# UPI-006: QR and fake cashback deception
URL: https://eyeinthesky6.github.io/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/qr-cashback-deception/
Description: UPI-006 — social engineering via deceptive QR codes, cashback claims, and tampered payment links.
Product: upi | Type: fraud-pattern | Review Stage: source-checked | Last Source Check: 2026-11-23
Actors: payer, tpap, psp-bank, remitter-bank, merchant | Evidence Layers: official, industry, research, atlas

## What it is
Fraudsters share QR codes or payment links promising cashbacks, refunds, prizes, or advance payments. Scanning the QR or tapping the link pre-fills an **outgoing payment** to an attacker-controlled VPA or merchant, so victims who enter their UPI PIN thinking they are "claiming" money authorize a debit instead. In a technical variant, attackers alter unsigned UPI deep-link parameters (`pa`, `pn`, `am`) to swap the payee or amount.

## Impact
- **Customer:** Instant unauthorized-looking loss even though the victim entered their PIN, creating complex dispute cases.
- **Bank & PSP:** Repeat scam complaints against newly spun-up or compromised payee VPAs and unsigned merchant links.
- **Merchant & App:** Tampered deep links erode checkout trust when payment amounts or displayed names diverge from orders.

## Common patterns
- **Fake cashback or reward QR:** Scammer sends a QR or link claiming cashback/prize credit upon UPI PIN entry.
- **Test-transfer doubling trick:** Fraudster blames a "system error" or "wrong account", asking for a small initial payment followed by larger transfers to unlock returns.
- **Tampered payment link:** Attackers rewrite payee address (`pa`) or amount (`am`) fields inside unsigned `upi://pay` links during checkout handoff.

## What to do (rules and mitigations)

| Basis | Owner | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory | Banks, NPCI ecosystem | Warn payers clearly that scanning a QR code and entering a UPI PIN is always for paying, never receiving money; show actual merchant names (not only intermediary aggregator names) on online transaction alerts and OTPs. |
| Regulatory | Commercial banks | Classify deception-induced approvals as fraudulent transactions (effective Jan 1, 2027), and record clear, directed scam warnings shown before confirmation. |
| Industry practice | PAs, Merchants, Apps | Digitally sign UPI payment links (`Signed Intent`) before app handoff so payee VPA and amount cannot be mutated mid-flow. |
| Research & academic | Risk engineering teams | Empirical GPay India study reports >88% recall when scoring initiation mode (`qr_scan`, `app_intent`, `payment_request`), memo text, payee history, and spam flags—but ~30% precision on evaluated splits makes hard auto-blocks too noisy without step-up or analyst review. |
| Atlas guidance | TPAPs, PSPs | Verify Signed Intent / Dynamic QR payloads server-side; surface prominent warnings when gallery-imported QR images or external links pay a new or previously reported VPA. |

## Watch-outs and validation
- **Legitimate lookalikes:** Genuine merchant cashback campaigns, dynamic POS QR checkouts, gallery-saved utility/kirana QR screenshots, and peer reimbursements.
- **Signals needed:** Initiation mode (`camera_qr`, `gallery_qr`, `external_intent`, `signed_intent`), payee VPA/MID/MCC, payee scam/spam report history, and payer-payee prior history.
- **How to validate:** Test rejection of unsigned or mutated `upi://pay` deep links in QA; measure user warning comprehension and false-positive drop-off on legitimate gallery QR retail payments before tightening friction.

## References and review history
1. NPCI, [Fraud Awareness](https://www.npci.org.in/fraud-awareness) (*Fake Cash back links* and *QR Codes* under *Fraud Trends against which users should be vigilant*), browser-checked Nov 23, 2026.
2. RBI, [Discussion Paper – Exploring safeguards in digital payments to curb frauds](https://www.rbi.org.in/scriptS/PublicationsView.aspx?id=23810) (Apr 9, 2026; non-binding consultation) — identifies social-engineering user manipulation as primary digital payment fraud driver (`§§iii, x`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
3. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13642), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/411` — merchant name visibility in online transaction alerts/OTPs (`§47`) and VPA/mobile-number monitoring parameters (`§53`), accessed Nov 23, 2026 (parallel `id=13624` PBs, `id=13633` SFBs).
4. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Responsible Business Conduct Third Amendment Directions, 2026](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13543&Mode=0), `RBI/2026-27/167` (Jun 24, 2026; effective Jan 1, 2027 for commercial banks excluding SFBs/PBs/RRBs/LABs) — `§§4(15A), 4(20C)(iii)`, accessed Nov 23, 2026.
5. Razorpay, [UPI Intent vs Collect: Which Flow Actually Works Better in 2026?](https://razorpay.com/blog/upi-intent-vs-collect-success-rates/) (Apr 9, 2026) — company-reported guide documenting `Signed Intent` payload verification, accessed Nov 23, 2026.
6. Dahiphale, D. et al. / Google, Inc. (2024), [Enhancing Trust and Safety in Digital Payments: An LLM-Powered Approach](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.19845v1), `arXiv:2410.19845v1` — empirical GPay India study (dataset/evaluation constraints prevent treating metrics as universal bank thresholds), accessed Nov 23, 2026.

**Review status:** NPCI Fraud Awareness, RBI, Razorpay, and `arXiv` sources checked 2026-11-23; independent reviewer: `PENDING`.

# UPI-007: Fake support and grievance impersonation
URL: https://eyeinthesky6.github.io/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/fake-support-impersonation/
Description: UPI-007 — search-result, social-media, and bogus call-centre impersonation around refunds and failed payments.
Product: upi | Type: fraud-pattern | Review Stage: source-checked | Last Source Check: 2026-11-23
Actors: payer, tpap, psp-bank, remitter-bank, payment-aggregator | Evidence Layers: official, atlas

## What it is
Customers dealing with a `PENDING` transfer, failed order, or delayed refund often search Google or post complaints on social media looking for helpline numbers. Scammers plant fake customer-care numbers in search ads, hijack brand support replies online, or run bogus call centres impersonating banks, TPAPs, or merchants—then collect OTPs/PINs, push remote-access apps, or coach victims into "refund verification" debits.

The root failure mode is **unclear in-app resolution status**, pushing anxious customers outside the app onto open web search.

## Impact
- **Customer:** A minor technical delay turns into full account compromise or secondary APP scam losses.
- **Bank, TPAP & PA:** Double burden of handling both the original transaction query and subsequent fraud reports/NCRP complaints.
- **Brand trust:** Poisoned search listings and fake handles damage confidence in official support channels.

## Common patterns
- **Search-ad customer care poisoning:** Sponsored or spoofed phone numbers appear above genuine bank/merchant help pages when a customer searches for refund help.
- **Social-media complaint hijacking:** Fraudsters watch public posts mentioning bank names, phone numbers, or UTRs and call victims pretending to resolve the ticket.
- **Bogus call-centre coaching:** Callers cite real-sounding transaction context or promise instant reversal if the victim enters a PIN or installs support software.

## What to do (rules and mitigations)

| Basis | Owner | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory | Banks, TPAPs | Provide a visible in-app grievance & failed-transaction dispute section with unique tracking IDs (under RBI ODR rules for TPAPs and digital security directions for banks); route fraud/unauthorized claims to the customer's bank. |
| Regulatory | Commercial banks | Maintain 24x7 fraud reporting channels, put direct reporting links on home pages and mobile apps, add SMS-reply objection numbers inside alerts, and advise customers to report via NCRP / 1930 (effective Jan 1, 2027). |
| Regulatory | Non-bank PSOs | Offer an in-app/website mark-fraud option, 24x7x365 customer and law-enforcement resolution desk, and active anti-phishing / anti-rogue-app monitoring and takedown services. |
| Atlas guidance | TPAPs, PSPs, PAs | Show live settlement/auto-reversal status (`T+1` / `T+5` timers) and 1-tap dispute reporting right on the transaction screen so users never need to search the web for help numbers. |
| Atlas guidance | Banks, TPAPs, PAs | Continuously take down impersonating search ads, social handles, and spoofed support domains; reinforce that official support never asks for PINs, OTPs, or screen sharing. |

## Watch-outs and validation
- **Legitimate lookalikes:** Genuine outbound calls from merchant logistics or outsourced support teams following up on orders. Focus defenses on clarity inside official apps, fast brand-impersonation takedowns, and flagging outbound transfers initiated right after a failed payment.
- **Signals needed:** Brand/domain monitoring alerts, in-app dispute funnel drop-off telemetry, complaint origin tags (`in-app` vs `NCRP/1930` vs `call centre`), and post-failure outbound payment timing.
- **How to validate:** Measure the share of failed-payment inquiries resolved in-app vs external channels, audit takedown turnaround times for fake handles/sites, and run end-to-end tests on 24x7 fraud reporting links.

## References and review history
1. NPCI, [Fraud Awareness](https://www.npci.org.in/fraud-awareness) (*Search Carried through Internet Search Engines*; *Users posting their potential Grievances on Social media platforms*), browser-checked Nov 23, 2026.
2. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13642), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/411` — clear in-app grievance section (`§59`) and ODR adherence (`§60`), accessed Nov 23, 2026 (parallel `id=13624` PBs, `id=13633` SFBs).
3. RBI, [Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) System for Digital Payments](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=11946&Mode=0), `RBI/2020-21/21` (Aug 6, 2020) — mandatory TPAP in-app dispute lodging (`Annex §5.2`) and unique reference tracking (`§5.4`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
4. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Responsible Business Conduct Third Amendment Directions, 2026](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13543&Mode=0), `RBI/2026-27/167` (Jun 24, 2026; effective Jan 1, 2027 for commercial banks excluding SFBs/PBs/RRBs/LABs) — 24x7 reporting links, alert reply numbers, and NCRP/1930 guidance (`§76G`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
5. RBI, [Master Directions on Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank PSOs](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13751&Mode=0), `RBI/DPSS/2026-27/475` (Nov 5, 2026; Large/Medium immediate, Small Apr 1, 2028) — mark-fraud facility (`§30`), 24x7x365 desk (`§27(d)`), and anti-phishing/anti-rogue-app takedowns (`§27(h)`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
6. RBI, [Discussion Paper – Exploring safeguards in digital payments to curb frauds](https://www.rbi.org.in/scriptS/PublicationsView.aspx?id=23810) (Apr 9, 2026; non-binding consultation) — cites bogus call centres and impersonation in NCRP fraud patterns (`§xi`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
7. NPCI, [UPI FAQs](https://www.npci.org.in/faqs/upi) (official UPI Help Assistant and grievance process), browser-checked Nov 23, 2026.
8. NPCI, [Complaint Register](https://www.npci.org.in/complaint-register) (confirms unauthorised/fraud complaints go directly to the customer's bank), browser-checked Nov 23, 2026.

**Review status:** NPCI Fraud Awareness/FAQs/Complaint Register and RBI sources checked 2026-11-23; independent reviewer: `PENDING`.

# UPI-008: Untrusted app and remote-access risk
URL: https://eyeinthesky6.github.io/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/untrusted-app-access/
Description: UPI-008 — sideloaded APKs, screen mirroring, remote-access coercion, and mobile RASP controls.
Product: upi | Type: preventive-control | Review Stage: source-checked | Last Source Check: 2026-11-23
Actors: payer, tpap, psp-bank, remitter-bank | Evidence Layers: official, atlas

## What it solves
Prevents attackers from spying on UPI PIN entry, intercepting OTPs, hijacking taps via screen overlays, or tampering with mobile app binaries when victims are talked into sideloading fake APKs (disguised as KYC/reward apps) or opening live screen-sharing/remote-access tools during a payment.

## Impact when missing
- **Customer:** Fraudsters watch screen state in real time, steal SMS OTPs, or guide taps across authorization screens.
- **TPAPs & Banks:** High-severity unauthorized transfers happen from the customer's own bound handset, bypassing normal device-trust assumptions.

## When it applies
- Payments initiated while live screen-mirroring, casting, or remote-access sessions are running.
- UPI apps sideloaded outside verified official app stores, on rooted/jailbroken devices, or with active USB debugging/instrumentation hooks (e.g., Frida).
- Coercion flows combining an active voice call with screen sharing or SMS-forwarding apps.

## What to do (rules and controls)

| Basis | Owner | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory | Commercial, Payments & Small Finance banks | Detect remote-access apps and block login access; verify secure download/install integrity, publish official app checksums, explore root/jailbreak install blocks, and consider anti-malware defenses. |
| Regulatory | Non-bank PSOs | Block mobile payment access whenever a remote-access session is live, and subscribe to anti-phishing and rogue-app takedown monitoring services. |
| Regulatory | NPCI ecosystem guidance | Public NPCI guidance warns users against downloading unknown APKs, screen-sharing tools, or SMS-forwarding apps, and advises not transacting during active calls. *(A separate NPCI 2025 mobile app security circular cited via bank mirror—specifying store install checks, screen-mirroring/USB-debug blocks, OTP auto-read, and runtime alerts—awaits public NPCI circular listing.)* |
| Atlas guidance | TPAPs, PSPs | Terminate or block UPI payment initiation whenever live screen mirroring, active casting, or remote control is detected, showing plain-language instructions on why access paused. |
| Atlas guidance | Mobile security & engineering | Enforce app-store signature verification, root/emulator/debugger detection, and overlay defense (`FLAG_SECURE` / non-obscured touch checks) without breaking OS accessibility tools. |

## Watch-outs and validation
- **Legitimate lookalikes (accessibility warning):** Screen readers used by visually impaired customers (`TalkBack`, `VoiceOver`), developer options enabled on personal test devices, corporate MDM support, and smart-TV casting. Target **active screen projection or remote-control sessions** rather than blanket-blocking all OS accessibility flags.
- **Signals needed:** OS accessibility and screen-projection/cast states, installer-source & package-signature checks, debugger/root/emulator flags, OTP sender-ID validation, and runtime SOC alerts.
- **How to validate:** Test active screen-mirroring, USB-debug, and overlay attacks in Android/iOS labs; verify `TalkBack`/`VoiceOver` accessibility compatibility so disabled users are never locked out; audit false-positive launch block rates.

## References and review history
1. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13642), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/411` (updated Oct 1, 2026) — secure install/checksums/remote-access login blocks (`§68(2)(ii),(iv), §68(4)–(5), §68(12)`), accessed Nov 23, 2026 (parallel `id=13624` PBs, `id=13633` SFBs).
2. RBI, [Master Directions on Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank PSOs](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13751&Mode=0), `RBI/DPSS/2026-27/475` (Nov 5, 2026; Large/Medium immediate, Small Apr 1, 2028) — rogue-app takedown (`§27(h)`) and blocking payments during live remote access (`§31(f)`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
3. NPCI circular `NPCI/2025-26/IS/003` (May 19, 2025), *Comprehensive Mobile Application Security Framework for UPI - 2025* — [provisional third-party bank mirror](https://rscb.bank.in/Content/pdf/npcicircular.pdf) (inspected pp. 1–8 covering Mandatory store/root/screen-mirror/USB-debug/OTP controls `A.1–2, B.12/14/15/23, C.1, D.1` and Recommended harmful-app/emulator/Frida/keylogger/overlay controls `A.3–4, B.19–21`; **remains provisional draft pending public `npci.org.in` listing**).
4. NPCI, [Fraud Awareness](https://www.npci.org.in/fraud-awareness) (*Downloading of unknown apps*), browser-checked Nov 23, 2026.
5. NPCI, [UPI Circulars index](https://www.npci.org.in/circulars/upi), browser-checked Nov 23, 2026 (confirmed `NPCI/2025-26/IS/003` is not listed on public `/circulars/upi` or `/circulars/others`).

**Review status:** RBI sources and `npci.org.in/fraud-awareness` checked 2026-11-23; `NPCI/2025-26/IS/003` absent from public `npci.org.in` circular indexes (provisional bank mirror used; stays `draft`); independent reviewer: `PENDING`.

# UPI-009: Authentication and payment authorization
URL: https://eyeinthesky6.github.io/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/authentication-context/
Description: UPI-009 — multi-factor authentication, dynamic factors, exemptions, and issuer responsibility.
Product: upi | Type: preventive-control | Review Stage: source-checked | Last Source Check: 2026-11-23
Actors: payer, tpap, psp-bank, remitter-bank | Evidence Layers: official, atlas

## What it solves
Ensures payment approvals genuinely come from the authorized customer and bound device rather than replayed credentials, stolen static passwords, or man-in-the-middle (MITM) tampering—while keeping exempted fast flows (like recurring mandates and Tap-and-Pay NFC UPI) correctly scoped.

## Impact when missing
- **Customer & Issuer:** Stolen static credentials or intercepted sessions let attackers authorize debits without clear merchant confirmation on alerts or OTPs.
- **Product teams:** Misreading RBI exemptions causes either broken checkout flows or non-compliant skip-auth bugs.

## When it applies
- Every domestic digital payment authorization unless explicitly covered by an active RBI two-factor exemption.
- High-risk sessions showing new geo, velocity, or payee changes suited for adaptive authentication.
- Mobile/web handshakes prone to TLS/session tampering.

## What to do (rules and controls)

| Basis | Owner | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory | Payment System Providers & Participants | Require at least two distinct authentication factors per transaction, including at least one dynamically generated/proven factor for non-card-present payments; recognize active exemptions (e.g., subsequent recurring e-mandates and NFC Tap-and-Pay UPI on POS). Issuers bear responsibility for compliance and may apply risk-based checks. |
| Regulatory | Commercial, Payments & Small Finance banks | Implement phishing/keylogger-resistant MFA, optional risk-based adaptive auth, SMS/email alerts for transactions and new linkages showing the actual merchant name (not only the PA), and MITM controls terminating interfered sessions. |
| Regulatory | Non-bank PSOs | Place OTP codes (where used) at the end of messages alongside the specific transaction reference, and preserve intact session security and encryption across mobile channels. |
| Atlas guidance | TPAPs, Remitter banks, PSPs | Cryptographically bind UPI PIN and device factor proofs to the exact amount, payee VPA/MID, and session integrity; terminate transactions immediately on TLS pinning or runtime tamper failures. |

## Watch-outs and validation
- **Legitimate lookalikes:** Exempted low-value NFC Tap-and-Pay UPI transactions, subsequent recurring e-mandate debits, and adaptive step-ups during genuine cross-city travel. Avoid dropping valid sessions solely on transient weak cellular handoffs.
- **Signals needed:** Auth factors verified (`PIN`, biometric, device token, exempt mandate/NFC), session TLS/pinning telemetry, merchant descriptor fields, and risk-based step-up audit logs.
- **How to validate:** Audit `Annexure-1` exemption flags against live product behavior, verify TLS error termination, and inspect live SMS/OTP alert templates for merchant-name display and end-placed OTP format.

## References and review history
1. RBI, [Authentication Mechanisms for Digital Payment Transactions Directions, 2025](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12898&Mode=0), `RBI/2025-26/79` (Sep 25, 2025; compliance by Apr 1, 2026) — scope (`§4`), 2FA + dynamic factor (`§6`), risk-based & issuer responsibility (`§§8–9`), and exemptions including recurring e-mandates and Tap-and-Pay UPI (`Annexure-1`, citing Sep 2, 2026 letter `CO.DPSS.POLC.No. S-550/02-23-001/2026-27`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
2. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13642), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/411` (updated Oct 1, 2026) — MFA, adaptive auth, merchant-name alerts, MITM termination (`§§42–49, 68(13)`), accessed Nov 23, 2026 (parallel `id=13624` PBs, `id=13633` SFBs).
3. RBI, [Master Directions on Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank PSOs](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13751&Mode=0), `RBI/DPSS/2026-27/475` (Nov 5, 2026; Large/Medium immediate, Small Apr 1, 2028) — OTP formatting (`§29(c)`) and mobile session/encryption protection (`§31(b)`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.

**Review status:** RBI primary sources checked 2026-11-23; independent reviewer: `PENDING`.

# UPI-010: Transaction velocity and EFRM monitoring
URL: https://eyeinthesky6.github.io/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/transaction-velocity/
Description: UPI-010 — regulatory Enterprise Fraud Risk Management (EFRM) architecture, alert parameterization, staff calibration, and feedback loops.
Product: upi | Type: detective-control | Review Stage: source-checked | Last Source Check: 2026-11-23
Actors: remitter-bank, beneficiary-bank, psp-bank, payment-aggregator | Evidence Layers: official, industry, research, atlas

## What it solves
Moves fraud monitoring beyond single heuristic alerts to a calibrated **monitoring program**: choosing governed rule parameters, sizing daily alert queues to analyst capacity, preventing biased rule feedback loops, and training operations teams to tell true fraud apart from benign activity. *(For account-level outbound burst features, see [Unusual outbound payment velocity (`UPI-001`)](/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/unusual-outbound-velocity/).)*

## Impact when missing
- **Fraud ops & analysts:** Poorly tuned alerts drown investigators in false positives while real attacks slip through unreviewed queues.
- **Legitimate merchants & users:** Naive static cutoffs trigger unexplained blocks, slow unblocking delays, and Ombudsman escalations.
- **Model drift:** Using uninvestigated past alerts as "clean" labels creates circular blind spots over time.

## When it applies
- Designing, updating, or auditing parameter sets in bank or PSO Enterprise Fraud Risk Management (EFRM) systems.
- Sizing analyst review queues and measuring true alert yield vs false-positive friction.
- Operating formal fraud investigation, root-cause review, and customer notice workflows.

## What to do (rules and controls)

| Basis | Owner | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory | Commercial, Payments & Small Finance banks | Document suspicious-behavior parameters (velocity, new beneficiaries, first-time app use, high-risk MCCs, new-account activity, time-zone/geo/rogue-IP, fraud-linked VPAs/mobiles, declines, missing approval codes), run root-cause analysis, train analysts specifically to distinguish false positives from true fraud, and keep ecosystem escalation SOPs current. |
| Regulatory | Commercial, Payments & Small Finance banks | Maintain Data Analytics/MI units monitoring digital transactions alongside EWS/RFA, and follow natural-justice due process (minimum 21-day Show Cause Notice and reasoned order) before formal fraud classification. |
| Regulatory | Non-bank PSOs | Operate a real-time/near-real-time fraud monitoring solution and share online alerts across participants for failed transactions, velocity, and new-account spikes (Large/Medium immediate; Small Apr 1, 2028). |
| Industry practice | Risk & rule teams | Backtest candidate rules before activation to balance fraud caught vs false blocks, allowing 60–120 day maturity windows so delayed chargebacks/disputes are not mislabeled clean *(method drawn from Stripe Radar guidance—do not copy non-India card thresholds)*. |
| Research & academic | ML & fraud ops teams | Benchmark models at realistic daily queue budgets (`k=100` vs `k=500` alerts, RBIH NFPC study) rather than arbitrary score cutoffs; pairing calibrated GBDTs with SHAP attributions and structured analyst narratives lifted investigator alert yield from 61% to 89% in an OCBC Singapore study (international comparison, not turnkey India rules). |
| Atlas guidance | Fraud engineering teams | Tag analyst dispositions cleanly (`confirmed_fraud`, `confirmed_false_positive`, `inconclusive`, `delayed_ncrp`) so offline retraining never treats cleared backlog as clean behavior. |

## Watch-outs and validation
- **Legitimate lookalikes:** High-volume micro-merchants, payroll runs, festival transfers, and housing-society or cooperative collections routinely breach naive static thresholds.
- **Signals needed:** Unified transaction + auth + device logs, rule-trigger history, timestamped analyst dispositions, delayed NCRP/chargeback outcomes, and customer segment tags (`retail` vs `merchant`).
- **How to validate:** Replay rules in observe-only (shadow) mode before turning on hard blocks; track `precision@k`, false-positive overturn rate, analyst handling time, and time-to-unblock for erroneous alerts.

## References and review history
1. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13642), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/411` (updated Oct 1, 2026) — documented config, alert parameters, root-cause fraud analysis, staff FP training, and SOPs (`Ch. I §3, §§52–56`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
2. RBI, [Payments Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13624), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/429` (updated Oct 1, 2026; `Ch. I §3, §§52–56`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
3. RBI, [Small Finance Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13633) (updated Oct 1, 2026; `Ch. I §3, §§52–56`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.

# UPI-011: Repeated failed authentication attempts
URL: https://eyeinthesky6.github.io/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/failed-authentication/
Description: UPI-011 — detecting credential stuffing, wrong-PIN probing, lockouts, and customer alerts.
Product: upi | Type: detective-control | Review Stage: source-checked | Last Source Check: 2026-11-23
Actors: payer, tpap, psp-bank, remitter-bank | Evidence Layers: official, atlas

## What it solves
Catches brute-force PIN/OTP guessing, stolen-device probing, or a coerced victim mistyping credentials—while separating real security failures from harmless CBS timeouts or poor mobile network drops so genuine users aren't trapped in dead-end lockouts.

## Impact when missing
- **Security exposure:** Unlimited retries allow automated probing or stolen-device guessing until an account compromises.
- **Customer friction:** Treating switch timeouts or connectivity errors like wrong-PIN attacks locks legitimate users out during urgent payments.

## When it applies
- Sequential wrong UPI PIN, invalid OTP, or failed mobile-app login attempts inside a short time window.
- Failed-auth spikes paired with unfamiliar devices, new VPAs, or IP changes.
- Reactivation flows after temporary security lockouts.

## What to do (rules and controls)

| Basis | Owner | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory | Commercial, Payments & Small Finance banks | Enforce a maximum limit on failed login/authentication attempts before blocking access; alert customers on failed attempts, maintain a secure reactivation process, and monitor declined transactions and invalid-PIN/credential strings as fraud parameters. |
| Regulatory | Non-bank PSOs | Enforce maximum failed login/auth attempts before locking app access, notify customers, keep a secure reactivation flow, and share participant failed-transaction alerts (Large/Medium immediate; Small Apr 1, 2028). |
| Atlas guidance | Remitter banks, PSPs, TPAPs | Separate `WRONG_PIN` / `INVALID_OTP` security errors from `TIMEOUT`, `SWITCH_DOWN`, or `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` technical declines so connectivity retries never count toward lockouts. |
| Atlas guidance | Remitter banks, TPAPs | Send instant out-of-band SMS/email alerts on failed auth lockouts, and escalate priority when wrong-PIN bursts coincide with new devices or unfamiliar payees. |

## Watch-outs and validation
- **Legitimate lookalikes:** Mistyped PINs by rushed or elderly users, poor mobile coverage causing user retries, accessibility input errors, or forgotten credentials right after reinstalling an app. Always provide a clear, documented reactivation path instead of a dead end.
- **Signals needed:** Normalized decline codes (`WRONG_PIN` vs `TIMEOUT` vs `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`), consecutive/windowed failure counts per account, device, and IP, and reactivation audit logs.
- **How to validate:** Test lockout counters and reactivation flows in QA staging, confirm customer alert delivery on failed attempts, and track wrong-PIN lockouts against confirmed ATO/fraud incidents.

## References and review history
1. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13642), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/411` (updated Oct 1, 2026) — failed-attempt lockout, reactivation & alerts, monitoring (`§§50–53`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
2. RBI, [Payments Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13624), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/429` (updated Oct 1, 2026; `§§50–53`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
3. RBI, [Small Finance Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13633) (updated Oct 1, 2026; `§§50–53`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
4. RBI, [Master Directions on Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank PSOs](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13751&Mode=0), `RBI/DPSS/2026-27/475` (Nov 5, 2026; `§§3, 28, 31(e)`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.

**Review status:** RBI primary sources checked 2026-11-23; independent reviewer: `PENDING`.

# UPI-012: Merchant onboarding and classification
URL: https://eyeinthesky6.github.io/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/merchant-onboarding/
Description: UPI-012 — Payment Aggregator KYC/CDD, MCC classification, acquiring bank oversight, and transaction laundering risks.
Product: upi | Type: preventive-control | Review Stage: source-checked | Last Source Check: 2026-11-23
Actors: payment-aggregator, beneficiary-bank, psp-bank, merchant | Evidence Layers: official, atlas

## What it solves
Stops shell businesses, banned merchants, and mule networks from acquiring P2M UPI handles through weak identity checks, misstated business descriptions (MCC miscoding), unregistered marketplace sub-merchants ("transaction laundering"), or settlement routing into unrelated third-party accounts.

## Impact when missing
- **Ecosystem & acquirers:** Fraud proceeds flow through misclassified merchant VPAs while regulators and acquiring banks hold ultimate oversight liability.
- **Customers:** Payers see confusing intermediary PA names instead of who they actually paid, aiding checkout deception and dispute delays.

## When it applies
- Onboarding any online, physical, or cross-border merchant via a Payment Aggregator (PA) or PSP bank.
- Onboarded marketplaces hosting third-party sellers or sub-merchants.
- Ongoing post-activation monitoring when live transaction size, volume, or domain diverges from the declared business profile.

## What to do (rules and controls)

| Basis | Owner | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory | Bank & non-bank PAs, Acquiring banks | Perform full KYC/CDD (CKYCR with consent, or PAN + physical Contact Point Verification + OVD/e-document), run background/antecedent & security checks, assign accurate MCC/MID/TID/name, forbid payments for un-onboarded marketplace sellers, settle only into the merchant's own verified bank account, monitor ongoing profile drift, and (for non-bank PAs) register with FIU-IND. Acquiring banks must enforce policy oversight even when PAs execute CDD. |
| Regulatory | Commercial, Payments & Small Finance banks | Display the actual merchant name (not only the intermediary PA) on customer alerts/OTPs for online payments, and include high-risk MCCs in transaction monitoring parameters. |
| Atlas guidance | PAs, PSP banks, Acquirers | Verify business category against live app/website/CPV evidence and confirm bank account ownership match before enabling live UPI acceptance. |
| Atlas guidance | PA risk teams | Alert on ticket-size jumps, odd-hour bursts, domain/IP changes, or refund spikes relative to the assigned MCC so transaction laundering is caught early. |

## Watch-outs and validation
- **Legitimate lookalikes:** Seasonal retailers during festive/wedding peaks, fast-growing D2C startups, and multi-line businesses legitimately adding categories. Sudden unexplained onboarding rejections or payout holds harm genuine SMBs—pair profile alerts with fast merchant verification outreach.
- **Signals needed:** KYC/CKYCR/PAN/CPV verification state, assigned MCC/MID/TID, verified settlement bank account match, live domain/app telemetry, ticket-size distribution, and dispute rates.
- **How to validate:** Sample-audit onboarded merchants for CPV and MCC accuracy, run negative tests on mismatched settlement accounts, and compare profile-drift alert yield against confirmed laundering exits.

## References and review history
1. RBI, [Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregator (PA)](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=12896), `RBI/DPSS/2025-26/141` (Sep 15, 2025; updated Nov 11, 2026) — PA scope (`§3`), KYC/CPV/background checks/MCC/marketplaces/settlement account/FIU-IND (`§13(a)–(i)`, `§13(j)` transition, `Annexure-1 §1.4`), and acquiring bank oversight (`§14`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
2. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13642), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/411` (updated Oct 1, 2026) — merchant name on alerts (`§47`) and high-risk MCC monitoring (`§53`), accessed Nov 23, 2026 (parallel `id=13624` PBs, `id=13633` SFBs).

**Review status:** RBI primary sources checked 2026-11-23 (`npci.org.in/product/upi/roles-responsibilities` confirms PSP banks onboard merchants; no separate public NPCI merchant-onboarding circular found on `/circulars/upi`); independent reviewer: `PENDING`.

# UPI-013: UPI dispute and complaint routing
URL: https://eyeinthesky6.github.io/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/dispute-routing/
Description: UPI-013 — RBI Online Dispute Resolution (ODR), PA chargeback/dispute flows, and separating failed vs. fraudulent incidents.
Product: upi | Type: recovery-process | Review Stage: source-checked | Last Source Check: 2026-11-23
Actors: payer, tpap, psp-bank, remitter-bank, beneficiary-bank, payment-aggregator, npci | Evidence Layers: official, industry, atlas

## What it solves
Ensures UPI complaints reach the right operational track immediately instead of landing in one generic support queue: separating (1) **failed/pending technical debits**, (2) **merchant non-delivery/refund disputes**, and (3) **unauthorized or scam-coerced transfers**.

## Impact when misrouted
- **Customers:** Delayed `T+1`/`T+5` ODR auto-reversals or missed urgent NCRP/1930 fraud reporting windows.
- **Merchants & PAs:** Routine order returns flagged as fraud disputes risk unjustified settlement holds or VPA blocks.
- **Banks:** Missed 15-day URCS response windows convert disputes into automatic *Deemed Accepted* chargeback losses.

## Where it applies
- **Technical failure:** Account debited without beneficiary/merchant credit → rule-based ODR (`T+1` / `T+5` SLA).
- **Merchant dispute:** Paid order failed fulfilment/refund → PA/acquirer evidence workflow (invoice, delivery proof).
- **Fraud / Unauthorized / Scam:** Instant 24x7 bank/PSO intake, "mark transaction as fraudulent" flag, NCRP/1930 routing, and URCS Fraud chargeback.

## What to do (rules and workflows)

| Basis | Owner | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory | Authorised PSOs, PSPs, TPAPs | Run rule-based, minimal-intervention ODR for failed transactions aligned to `T+1`/`T+5` compensation TATs; TPAPs must embed in-app grievance lodging with unique tracking IDs (unresolved claims >1 month escalate to RBI Integrated Ombudsman). |
| Regulatory | Commercial, PB, SFB banks & PSOs | Provide an explicit in-app grievance section with timelines plus an authenticated "mark/identify transaction as fraudulent" option; commercial banks (effective Jan 1, 2027) must run 24x7 fraud reporting, SMS-reply alert objection numbers, direct links, NCRP/1930 guidance, and immediate acknowledgement. |
| Regulatory | Payment Aggregators, NPCI ecosystem | Maintain a published dispute policy, refund SLA, escalation matrix, and grievance officer with acquirers/merchants. Under NPCI rules, unauthorized/fraud claims go to the customer's bank (`Chargeback -> Re-present -> Pre-Arbitration -> Arbitration`), with **15 calendar days** in URCS for Fraud/Wrong Credit chargeback responses before automatic *Deemed Accepted* closure. |
| Industry practice | PAs, Merchants | Track disputes cleanly across phases (*Fraud*, *Retrieval*, *Chargeback*, *Pre-Arbitration*, *Arbitration*) and statuses (`Open`, `Under Review`, `Won`, `Lost`, `Closed`) via webhooks and portal workflows to submit delivery/invoice proof or refund promptly *(Razorpay documented pattern)*. |
| Atlas guidance | TPAPs, Banks, PAs | Build 3-way intake classification right on the transaction screen—routing unsettled debits to ODR/TAT timers, fulfilment issues to PA evidence queues, and scam/ATO reports directly to 24x7 fraud desks + NCRP/1930 guidance. |

## Watch-outs and validation
- **Legitimate lookalikes:** Temporary `PENDING` transactions awaiting clearing, user-cancelled retries, and normal merchant return/exchange requests should never be tagged as fraud disputes.
- **Signals needed:** RRN/UTR, switch/settlement state, unique ODR reference ID, merchant invoice/delivery proof, alert/report timestamps, and NCRP complaint ID linkage.
- **How to validate:** Audit unique ODR tracking generation, test 1-tap mark-fraud flows end-to-end, monitor unresolved tickets approaching the 30-day Ombudsman mark, and track approaching 15-day URCS deadlines.

## References and review history
1. RBI, [Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) System for Digital Payments](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=11946&Mode=0), `RBI/2020-21/21` (Aug 6, 2020) — rule-based ODR, TPAP in-app facility (`Annex §5.2`), unique tracking ref (`§5.4`), Ombudsman 1-month escalation (`§4`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
2. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13642), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/411` — app grievance section (`§§59–60`) and mark-fraud button (`§66`), accessed Nov 23, 2026 (parallel `id=13624` PBs, `id=13633` SFBs, `Id=13751 §30` non-bank PSOs).
3. RBI, [Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregator (PA)](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=12896), `RBI/DPSS/2025-26/141` (updated Nov 11, 2026; `§8`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
4. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Responsible Business Conduct Third Amendment Directions, 2026](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13543&Mode=0), `RBI/2026-27/167` (effective Jan 1, 2027 for commercial banks excluding SFBs/PBs/RRBs/LABs; `§§76G, 76I`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
5. NPCI, [UPI Settlement Process](https://www.npci.org.in/uploads/UPI_Settlement_Process_256f73e1df.pdf) (`§4 Dispute Resolution Mechanism`, p. 4 ODR summary; undated 4 pp. public PDF), browser-checked Nov 23, 2026.

# UPI-014: Settlement and reconciliation exceptions
URL: https://eyeinthesky6.github.io/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/settlement-exceptions/
Description: UPI-014 — interbank settlement-file reconciliation, failed-transaction TATs, and scheme exception handling.
Product: upi | Type: operational-failure | Review Stage: source-checked | Last Source Check: 2026-11-23
Actors: remitter-bank, beneficiary-bank, psp-bank, npci | Evidence Layers: official, atlas

## What it is
Even when merchant checkouts handle webhooks properly ([Payment status and order reconciliation](/india-fintech-risk-atlas/upi/payment-status-reconciliation/)), clearing breaks occur at the **interbank switch and settlement layer**: a customer's account gets debited while the beneficiary bank fails to credit (`UDIR`/timeout), settlement files carry unmatched RRNs/UTRs, or reversals miss statutory deadlines.

## Impact
- **Customer:** Held debit funds awaiting manual intervention or delayed `₹100/day` failed-transaction compensation.
- **Beneficiary & remitter banks:** Unreconciled breaks create deemed-accepted chargeback losses once NPCI's shortened 15-day URCS TAT expires.
- **Wrongful freezes:** Treating routine settlement timing lags as suspected fraud unnecessarily locks accounts.

## Common failure modes
- **Unmatched clearing/CBS legs:** Core banking debits post without matching NPCI clearing confirmation within 24 hours.
- **Segregated dispute cycle lag:** AUTH cycles (`1–10`) separate cleanly from Dispute Cycles (`DC1`, `DC2`) and `DR` reports, so ignoring `DR` adjustment files leaves exceptions unresolved.
- **Missed URCS chargeback TAT:** Beneficiary banks failing to accept or reject Fraud/Wrong Credit chargebacks within **15 calendar days** lose automatically via *Deemed Accepted* closure.

## What to do (rules and controls)

| Basis | Owner | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Regulatory | Commercial, Payments & Small Finance banks | Run real-time/near-real-time reconciliation across all ecosystem participants (PSOs, aggregators, processors) within **<= 24 hours of receiving settlement files** to catch suspicious or mismatched activity. *(Note: governs inter-entity reconciliation timing, distinct from customer reversal SLAs.)* |
| Regulatory | Remitter & beneficiary banks, Non-bank PSOs | Auto-reverse debited-but-uncredited **P2P** transfers by `T+1` calendar day and unconfirmed **merchant (P2M)** payments by `T+5` calendar days (`₹100/day` *suo motu* compensation after expiry), crediting customers the same day funds arrive from beneficiary side. Keep PA day-end escrow >= merchant payables. |
| Regulatory | NPCI member banks | Reconcile segregated AUTH cycles (`1–10`) separately from Dispute Cycles `DC1` (`00:00–16:00`), `DC2` (`16:00–00:00`), and non-settlement `DR` adjustment reports (`00:00–10:00`); respond to Fraud & Wrong Credit chargebacks in URCS within **15 calendar days** (reduced from 35) to prevent automatic *Deemed Accepted* closure. |
| Atlas guidance | Clearing & recon engineering | Run automated 3-way matching (CBS ledger + switch response logs + clearing/DR files) within the <= 24h window, routing hanging debits straight into `T+1`/`T+5` SLA trackers separately from fraud hold queues. |

## Watch-outs and validation
- **Legitimate lookalikes:** Asynchronous cycle cutoffs, deemed-approved/timeout switch responses, and merchant order-reference formatting mismatches are operational timing gaps, not fraud—never auto-freeze user accounts on unconfirmed recon breaks alone.
- **Signals needed:** RRN/UTR, NPCI response codes (`00`, `RB`, timeout/deemed-approved), cycle batch ID (`AUTH`/`DC1`/`DC2`/`DR`), CBS debit/credit timestamps, and PA escrow ledger rows.
- **How to validate:** Test end-of-cycle unmatched files and `T+1`/`T+5` compensation triggers in recon QA; track daily `<= 24h` reconciliation SLA breaches and approaching 15-day URCS deadlines.

## References and review history
1. RBI, [Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13642), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/411` (updated Oct 1, 2026) — `<= 24h` inter-entity reconciliation framework (`§57`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
2. RBI, [Payments Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13624), `RBI/DoS/2026-27/429` (updated Oct 1, 2026; `§57`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
3. RBI, [Small Finance Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13633) (updated Oct 1, 2026; `§57`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
4. RBI, [Harmonisation of Turn Around Time (TAT) and customer compensation for failed transactions](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=11693&Mode=0), `RBI/2019-20/67` (Sep 20, 2019; `§§4–6`, Sl. no. 4) — `T+1` P2P (`4(a)`), `T+5` merchant (`4(b)`), same-day credit (`§5`), `₹100/day` compensation, accessed Nov 23, 2026.
5. RBI, [Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregator (PA)](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=12896), `RBI/DPSS/2025-26/141` (updated Nov 11, 2026; `§§16, 18(h)`), accessed Nov 23, 2026.
6. NPCI, [UPI Settlement Process](https://www.npci.org.in/uploads/UPI_Settlement_Process_256f73e1df.pdf) (`§4 Dispute Resolution Mechanism`; undated 4 pp. public PDF) & [UPI Circulars index](https://www.npci.org.in/circulars/upi), browser-checked Nov 23, 2026.
7. NPCI, [`NPCI/2025-26/UPI/222A`: Addendum – Segregation of UPI Settlement Cycles for Auth and Disputes Transactions](https://www.npci.org.in/uploads/UPI_OC_No_222_A_FY_2025_26_Addendum_segregation_of_UPI_settlement_cycles_for_Auth_and_disputes_transactions_42766ab9aa.pdf) (Oct 29, 2025; effective Dec 15, 2025), browser-checked Nov 23, 2026.
8.
